projectTitle: SWARM - de novo minibinders against Deformed Wing Virus paired with multiplexed RNAi against Varroa destructor
tagline: Protecting honeybees by hitting both the virus and the mite that carries it, with the first reported minibinder confirmed to bind DWV's VP3.
summary: Lambert iGEM (Suwanee, Georgia) built SWARM to attack the two linked causes of honeybee colony collapse: Deformed Wing Virus and the Varroa destructor mite that vectors it. US beekeepers reported losing 55.6% of managed colonies between April 2024 and April 2025, and Georgia's large operations lost roughly 88,000 colonies in nine months. SWARM pairs a computationally designed 79-amino-acid minibinder against the exposed P-domain of DWV's VP3 capsid protein - experimentally confirmed by biolayer interferometry at KD = 603.6 nM (95% CI 497.1-733.3 nM), to the team's knowledge the first reported minibinder with confirmed binding to VP3 - with a multiplexed dsRNA construct silencing three Varroa salivary-gland genes (Vd-CHIsal, Vd-CHIBIN, VdAV422) at once to blunt resistance. Both components are delivered through feeding practices beekeepers already use. They took the High School Grand Prize plus Best Model, Best Wiki, Best Sustainable Development Impact and Best Village Project, and the modelling is the headline: four linked models spanning protein design benchmarking on 5,721 experimentally labelled designs, oral pharmacokinetics with Sobol sensitivity analysis, a 13-ODE RNAi network, and an individual-based six-year colony epidemiology simulation across two climates.
awards: Best Sustainable Development Impact winner (High School)
Best Village Project winner (Climate Crisis / Conservation / Bioremediation)

dry.frameworks: Four models, each doing distinct work. (1) Minibinder design. No de novo minibinder or validated minibinder epitope existed for DWV, so they compared isolated P-domain structures against the assembled capsid to assess which surfaces are actually accessible, and investigated five candidate epitopes (an initial C-terminal region at I405/F408, EP-1 at I302/Y359/R395, EP-2 at V322/Q325/Y346, the QP/A-ridge at Q325/P326, and a putative catalytic triad at H277/S278/D294). They benchmarked computational confidence metrics against 5,721 labelled designs across 41 protein targets (849 confirmed binders, 4,872 non-binders) using ROC-AUC: minimum ipSAE scored 0.806 and ipSAE 0.801 pooled, Boltz-2 ipTM only 0.628, and a combined 38-metric ensemble just 0.541 - barely above chance - so adding metrics did not help. They also found minimum ipSAE degrades when comparing designs within a single target, which is exactly their use case, so they built a filtering framework combining predicted interface quality, amino-acid composition, predicted aggregation propensity, independent monomer prediction and cross-tool agreement; the motivating evidence was a candidate whose repeated minimum ipSAE predictions ranged from 0.000 to 0.676. Designs were generated with three independent tools - Mosaic, BindCraft and BoltzProt - with Boltz and Protenix used for additional structural evaluation; across 1,176 pairwise comparisons the median Jaccard similarity between BindCraft and Mosaic target-contact residue sets was 0.000 and their predicted interface centres were a median 42.9 angstroms apart, proving the tools explore genuinely different surfaces. Round 1 submitted 15 designs and produced zero confirmed binders (including 5G51_V4_seed01 at ipSAE 0.927 and ipTM 0.958, which failed); Round 2 generated 103 candidate entries, submitted 20, and produced one confirmed binder, l79_s469532_mpnn9, a BindCraft design associated with the QP/A-ridge that notably did not have the highest minimum ipSAE in the batch. Total compute spend was under USD 400 across 35 tested candidates, which they contrast against the USD 10,000 GPU budget per single-target campaign in Anthropic's 2026 autonomous binder-design technical report. (2) Minibinder dosing. A two-compartment oral pharmacokinetic model following functional protein from feeder to crop to gut to hemolymph: dG/dt = R_crop(t) - (ka + kt + kg)G and dH/dt = kaG - khH, with crop emptying fitted from Fournier et al. as V_crop = max(0, 17.966 - 0.159 t_min) uL reaching zero at about 113 minutes, digestive half-lives sampled log-normally around 31 and 54 minute values measured for native Manse-AS peptide in Myzus persicae and Acyrthosiphon pisum aphid gut extracts, and circulating stability from a juvenile hormone esterase analogue. 1,000 parameter sets were simulated for a 40,000-bee colony over 56 days; at a selected 100 nM average circulating concentration the median requirement was 29.60 g prepared protein (0.529 g/day prepared, 0.447 g/day active swallowed). Sobol total-effect sensitivity indices on log10(course mass), from 1,024 base samples and 7,168 model evaluations, ranked circulating functional loss 0.606, digestive loss 0.263, gut absorption 0.116, hemolymph volume 0.018 and intestinal transit 0.005 - and they reported that the gram-scale analysis failed its numerical checks so only the log-scale ranking is given. (3) RNAi model. A 13-species, 23-reaction ODE network in MATLAB SimBiology covering Dicer-2 processing of multiplexed dsRNA into three siRNAs, Ago2 loading into RISC, RISC-mediated Michaelis-Menten cleavage of a targeted Renilla transcript, untargeted Firefly as the control, plus transcription, translation, plasmid dilution, protein turnover and free-RNA degradation, with every rate parameter tabulated against its source and explicitly labelled as a measurement, a team estimate or an assumption. Predicted signal decrease was 37.50% with one siRNA, 67.51% with two, 83.41% with three directly delivered siRNAs, and 83.04% with the multiplexed dsRNA construct - the key result, since it predicts that bundling three guides into one molecule preserves knockdown. Local normalised sensitivity put RISC-mediated cleavage (Vm_1) at -1.72, the dominant assumption, while free Ago2 was near zero. (4) Epidemiological model. An individual-based six-year daily simulation of a two-deep-box Langstroth hive with about 42,000 brood cells, tracking adult bees individually by age, task, infection status and relative syrup intake, and mites on adults individually with sealed-cell brood and mites grouped by developmental day. It composes published frameworks - Sumpter and Martin for mite-virus-colony dynamics, Khoury/Myerscough/Barron for the saturating colony-size term N/(w+N) and forager recruitment R = alpha - sigma(F/N), Betti/Wahl/Zamir for infection-driven mortality, BEEPOP and BEEHAVE for seasonal development and weather-dependent foraging, and Martin and Calis for mite development and transfer. Daily weather was generated from NOAA 1991-2020 climate normals and 2011-2020 daily records preserving warm/cold runs, with foraging requiring a dry day above 12.8 C; 20 matched weather sequences per scenario across Atlanta and Ithaca gave 800 six-year simulations. Minibinder protection enters per bee as p_i(t) = 1 - exp(-K x_i u(t)) calibrated to 52.6% mean reduction in infection probability at full uptake with a lognormal intake distribution (mean-to-median ratio 1.68, sigma 1.0214); RNAi enters as an exposure state dF_i/dt = k_u x_i u(t)(1 - F_i) - k_loss F_i feeding f_treated(t_c) = f_0[1 - r_max F(t_c)] at brood capping, with r_max = 93.6% from an external study reporting 0.13 offspring per treated mother mite versus 2.04 in control.
dry.dataviz: The Best Wiki award is earned by making the models inspectable rather than illustrated. The VP3 epitope map is an interactive 3D viewer with five selectable, labelled regions and a toggle to overlay the confirmed minibinder's predicted pose, backed by a table giving each region's residues, structural rationale and experimental outcome. All 35 submitted minibinder designs are published in a sortable, filterable, searchable table - by design round, by experimental result - with each row expandable to show ipTM, ipSAE (labelled as to whether it is directional minimum ipSAE), design region, BLI sensor loading, the assay note and the source record, plus a full CSV download; failures and 'no usable result' entries are given equal prominence to the one success. A separate full-screen minibinder viewer shows the VP3 and GFP designs. The epidemiological model has a clickable four-stage 'one day in the model' diagram, a weekly-resolution Colony Viewer, and location-switchable figure sets for Atlanta and Ithaca covering colony survival, annual pollination, per-crop pollination and crop bloom windows, with results expressed relative to a paired Varroa-free colony under matched weather. Sensitivity results are shown as Matplotlib SVGs with bootstrap error bars. PRINCE ships a local web application with an interactive Structural context panel showing geometry findings, assessment status and crystal-contact summaries with per-residue measurements, JSON and CSV export, and two screencast demo videos (web app and CLI). The Modeling Instructional Series is seven videos teaching other teams a four-stage workflow for turning wet-lab protocols into MATLAB SimBiology models.
dry.datascience: The defining habit is turning other people's experimental data into a decision rule, then keeping the honest ledger. PRINCE's antibody epitope ranker was trained on 6,937 experimentally observed antibody-antigen interfaces across 1,549 antigen clusters, split by antigen cluster with sequence-homology checks between train, validation and test; it scored a cluster-averaged top-three majority-hit rate of 50.8% across 251 test clusters against 23.3% random, and on the harder retrospective subset of 93 clusters with no training homolog at 30% sequence identity or above it scored 45.8% against 23.8% random. An earlier residue-level benchmark on 110 common interfaces gave PRINCE a macro AUROC of 0.6722 against BepiPred-3.0 at 0.6524 and PeSTo at 0.6521, and the lightweight web-app scorer was benchmarked separately at 0.648 against 0.645 for exposure alone - a near-null result they published. Separately they retrospectively analysed 1,307 experimentally tested minibinder designs across 15 targets and found that across the 13 targets evaluable for site-level comparison the best-performing site averaged a 64% success rate against a 32% target-wide average, meaning site choice roughly doubles the hit rate; ranking by surface exposure alone put the best site in the top three for 10 of 13 targets (77%) against about 49% random, reported p = 0.032. Reporter work was properly calibrated with linear fits RLU_R = 206,101[Rluc] + 70,894 and RLU_F = 624[Fluc] + 57.8. Model validation against external data is laid out as a side-by-side table of published observation versus model output with an interpretation column that repeatedly says the comparison does not constitute validation: simulated managed mite loads of 2.42 (Atlanta) and 1.26 (Ithaca) per 100 bees against the USDA APHIS National Honey Bee Survey mean of 4.14 in positive samples, 27.8% and 8.8% of colony-months above three mites per 100 bees against 41.7% of survey samples, median untreated survival of 2.1 and 2.0 years against a Finnish study's 4-5 years from low initial infestation, and a simulated mean autumn population of 285 mites (range 165-514) against an observed 340. Headline outcome: all untreated colonies were lost by the end of year three, while SWARM alone retained 96.7% of reference crop pollination in Atlanta and 94.7% in Ithaca at year six against 45.1% and 79.8% for amitraz under an assumed five-year decline in effectiveness, with SWARM ahead in all 20 paired simulations at each location. Under the chosen assumptions RNAi supplied most of the benefit and the minibinder a smaller increment - a conclusion that undercuts their own flagship protein work, and they say so.
dry.software: PRINCE (released open source) is the team's software tool: it ranks candidate binding sites on a user-supplied protein structure before any compute is spent on design, combining a trained site ranker over geometric, atomic and protein-language-model features with a lightweight structural surface scorer, a crystal-contact and geometry checker that compares a chain alone against its crystal surroundings to flag where neighbouring copies cover a proposed site and where sections are missing or atomic positions uncertain, and a literature-evidence layer. It ships as a locally run web application for interactive use and a CLI for automated workflows, with JSON/CSV export, documentation, a command-line reference and a reproduction guide. Model: https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/lambert-ga/prince-model ; web app: https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/lambert-ga/prince-webapp ; team repo: https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/lambert-ga. Hardware (Best Hardware nominee): Vapor-X, an automated vacuum dryer built on the Clausius-Clapeyron relation, using a 12 V vacuum pump to lower pressure in a sealed Mason jar while a flexible resistive heating pad gently warms the sample, controlled by a Raspberry Pi Pico W on a custom PCB with an OLED display and rotary encoder for target temperature, vacuum strength and drying time. Prototype components cost USD 80.07 (USD 95.52 including PCB assembly) against USD 5,000-25,000 for a benchtop lyophiliser. It was validated externally: testing at the University of Alabama at Birmingham recovered 38 of 43 measured compounds (88.4%) within 5% of undried controls, and testing at Georgia Institute of Technology showed GFP fluorescence comparable to controls after drying GFP DNA and cell lysates; internal Bradford-assay work and a classroom deployment assessed recovery and usability. Also released: the seven-video Modeling Instructional Series for teams with no modelling experience, and the full model result records and 1,000 paired parameter records for the dosing model as downloadable JSON and CSV.
stack: ipSAE / minimum ipSAE / ipTM / pLDDT confidence metrics
Jaccard similarity of interface contact sets
NOAA climate normals and daily records
techniques: benchmarking design-confidence metrics against thousands of labelled experimental outcomes instead of trusting them
detecting metric instability by repeating predictions on the same candidate
measuring tool diversity quantitatively (Jaccard 0.000, 42.9 angstrom interface separation) to justify using three design tools
site-level rather than design-level success analysis (best site 64% vs target-wide 32%)
cluster-split benchmarking with sequence-homology checks and a no-homolog retrospective subset
variance-based global sensitivity analysis with bootstrap intervals and disclosed failed numerical checks
paired-weather-sequence experimental design so treatments are compared under matched conditions
composing several published models into one individual-based simulation with per-framework attribution
separating measured inputs from assumed inputs in every parameter table
publishing all 35 tested designs including failures and unusable assays, with a CSV download
external third-party hardware validation at two universities

good.publicEngagement: Over 30 initiatives reaching more than 530 participants worldwide, organised around three stated principles (quality information, diversity and outreach, hands-on lessons) and mapped individually to UN SDGs. For elementary audiences they wrote and illustrated an original children's book, 'The Mite-ty Adventure of Bentley the Bee', for ages 5-9, iterated against feedback from elementary teachers, designed to be legible to readers with colour vision deficiencies, translated into 13 languages, read aloud to first-graders at Sharon Elementary, and now held in the Atlanta Botanical Garden's library as part of its pollinator education. They also ran a Sharon Elementary Critter Club workshop in which students learned pollination while physically preparing the plots of their own pollinator garden. For middle school they ran Riverwatch workshops and a week-long Biotech Bootcamp for 62 campers structured one day per iGEM committee, with candy DNA models, micropipetting, strawberry DNA extraction, a C. elegans RNAi feeding experiment observed under the microscope across the week, and a 'germiest place in school' swabbing experiment; pre/post survey comparisons were collected. For older audiences there were pollinator presentations, a high school debate, a Connectivity Night, webinars, a keynote at the NWGA RESA STEM for Tomorrow Forum, a Concrete Jungle workshop, a Gardener's Handbook with practical pollinator-friendly planting guidance, a Bee PSA, mentorship, and a GBA Fall Conference and mini jamboree. Two inclusivity programmes carry the Best Sustainable Development Impact award. Flowers for the Future partners with a non-profit supporting Afghan girls barred from school past sixth grade to obtain a GED; Lambert teaches a multi-week 'Intro to Synthetic Biology' course there (central dogma, units and dimensional analysis, DNA and mutations, gene expression, genetic engineering techniques including transformation, transfection, viral vectors and CRISPR, PCR and gel electrophoresis, experimental design, scientific writing, bioethics), now in its third semester and reaching about 120 students, with a linked FFF-BioBuilderClub. Exceptional Science! brings kinesthetic science lessons to the neurodivergent class at their own school - acid-base reactions, genetics, density, candy DNA models, a rainbow pinwheel density experiment - plus a honeybee/DWV movement game where students first forage freely as healthy bees and then may only hop, citing research that physical activity improves inhibition and rule-switching response times in children with ADHD; they also published a Neurodivergent Handbook.
good.ihp: IHP ran across four sequenced phases (food insecurity/agriculture/city planners, beekeepers, experts and professors, then policymakers and governmental organisations), with every interaction processed through a four-step cycle they call H.I.V.E. - Hear, Inquire, Validate, Evolve - and a hard rule that a cycle is incomplete unless it ends in a concrete change or a documented reason why no change was warranted. Each stakeholder is also tagged with the SDGs they bear on, which is how the SDG scoring on the Sustainability page is built. The pivots are named, dated and attributed on a published timeline. February 2026: Dr. Aashish Manglik (UCSF) told them computational nanobody discovery still needs libraries of hundreds to thousands of candidates - 'For our computational design projects, we still make libraries of hundreds or thousands of candidates' - so testing 10 to 50 would likely fail even with a correct pipeline, and pointed them at BindCraft and Protenix; the team abandoned nanobodies for minibinders, which changed the entire wet lab. July 2026: Dr. Morgane Golan prompted the move to Sf9 cells as the RNAi model system. August 2026: Tudor Cotet and Corey Howe of Adaptyv Bio told them to stop targeting the P-domain broadly and focus designs on specific binding hotspots, and Cotet reviewed the failed first campaign before round two. September 2026: Dr. Mark Styczynski (Georgia Tech) pushed them off over-specific model parameters onto literature-supported ones, which is why every parameter table now carries a source attribution and an honest label; and Samantha Houck's input added SDG 11 to their framework. Professors Benjamin Lamp and Tatsuhiko Kadowaki, both DWV specialists, narrowed the target to VP3's exposed P-domain and warned how hard epitope selection is without experimental binding data, which made epitope evaluation a first-class modelling step and directly motivated PRINCE - as did Dr. Michael Hecht (Princeton) emphasising the uncertainty of epitope selection. Professor Raymond Owens (Oxford / Rosalind Franklin Institute) reframed binder choice around production cost and failure rate. Entomologist Dr. Jeff Pettis answered the ecological question head-on, saying eliminating Varroa would be 'completely fine' because they are obligate parasites invasive to the US, which underpins the safety case; he also named the political context, that pollinators are undervalued and under-resourced. On the practice side, Peter Helfrich (President, Metro Atlanta Beekeepers Association) identified DWV as the most dangerous threat and stressed that treatments must not harm brood, which made brood safety an explicit project priority; board member Claressa Lucas supplied the line that frames the whole project, 'It's not a matter of if there are Varroa mites. Every colony has them.' Professor Lewis Bartlett (University of Georgia) endorsed sucrose solution as a practical delivery vehicle, and contacts associated with Norroa, the registered RNA-based Varroa treatment, informed the syrup-pouch format. Sharanya Madhavan of Concrete Jungle, after six months of conversations and a joint workshop, connected bee health to rising food insecurity and urban pollinator corridors, which reshaped the outreach programme.
good.realWorld: A business-to-business licensing strategy rather than a direct-sales fantasy: established agricultural biotechnology manufacturers would produce and distribute SWARM through existing commercial networks, priced at USD 39.99 per hive treatment against an estimated mature manufacturing cost of USD 25.00, targeting commercial beekeepers who supply pollination services to high-value agriculture. The plan models 300,000 annual treatments by 2034 (base case 150,000, long-term goal one million), giving roughly USD 12 million in retail sales and USD 525,000 in licensing royalties under a proposed 5% royalty, and is supported by TAM/SAM/SOM, market competition and SWOT analysis, an AIDA distribution model, beekeeper return-on-investment calculations, revenue and sales forecasts, manufacturing and operating expense breakdowns, break-even analysis and a risk-management section. The four-year plan is sequenced around the real regulatory gate: 2027 R&D, 2028 product optimisation and safety, 2029 field validation and partnerships, 2030 commercialisation preparation, with a manufacturing partner and pesticide registration secured before launch - sensible given Norroa/Vadescana was registered as a biopesticide in 2025 and is the obvious precedent. Vapor-X is handled as a separate commercialisation track, offered either through manufacturer licensing or open-source release to educational and research laboratories, with prototype and commercial manufacturing cost breakdowns and an explicit open-source contribution to future iGEM teams. Implementation is built around equipment beekeepers already own: dsRNA in a sealed flexible syrup pouch with an adhesive cover over proboscis-sized feeding openings placed in the brood box (modelled on the Norroa format, where worker bees redistribute syrup into brood stores and nurse bees incorporate it into brood food), and the minibinder as a dried packet mixed into sucrose solution and served through a standard hive-top feeder. Throughout, the team draws the line clearly: BLI established binding to a VP3 construct, not neutralisation of assembled virus; neither component has been tested in a honeybee colony; the 100 nM circulating concentration is a selected simulation value, not an established protective threshold; and the RNAi potency figure is an external conditional effect, not a measurement of SWARM's own construct. Impact is mapped through a 'Roots-to-Fruits' model linking seven SDGs - 2, 4, 5, 8, 11, 15 and 17.

gemsTakeaway: The transferable insight is that Lambert beat the metric rather than trusting it: they benchmarked ipSAE, ipTM and a 38-metric ensemble against 5,721 labelled experimental designs, found the ensemble barely beat chance (ROC-AUC 0.541) and that their eventual hit did not even have the best score, then showed with 1,307 prior designs that choosing the right epitope roughly doubles the hit rate (64% at the best site vs 32% target-wide) and released that insight as open-source software, PRINCE - landing the first confirmed DWV VP3 binder on under USD 400 of compute. A high-school-plus centre should copy that whole posture: cheap compute plus a public dataset plus honest benchmarking, and publish every tested candidate including the failures in a sortable, downloadable table.
